# `utils/ObjectPool.js`

> **Source:** `editor/js/utils/ObjectPool.js`

ObjectPool - Reusable object pools to reduce GC pressure Wraps engine's ObjectPool with editor-specific convenience functions. Uses engine pools where available, adds editor-specific pools. Supports: - Float32Array pools (for transforms, matrices) - Generic array pools - Vec3/Vec4 pools

## Functions

### `getFloat32Array(size)`

Get a Float32Array of specified size from pool

### `releaseFloat32Array(arr)`

Return a Float32Array to the pool

### `getArray()`

Get a generic array from pool

### `releaseArray(arr)`

Return a generic array to the pool

### `getVec3(x = 0, y = 0, z = 0)`

Get a vec3 [x, y, z] from pool

### `releaseVec3(v)`

Return a vec3 to pool

### `getVec4(x = 0, y = 0, z = 0, w = 1)`

Get a vec4 [x, y, z, w] from pool

### `releaseVec4(v)`

Return a vec4 to pool

### `getMat4()`

Get a mat4 (16 floats) from pool

### `releaseMat4(m)`

Return a mat4 to pool

### `getPoolStats()`

Get pool statistics

### `clearPools()`

Clear all pools (for memory pressure situations)

### `trimPools(keepRatio = 0.5)`

Trim pools to reduce memory (keep some for reuse)

## Constants

- `transformPool`
- `snapshotEntityPool`

## Notes & Examples

### Editor Extension System

The editor supports extensions via the same Plauna component system as apps. Extensions can add panels, tools, menu items, and hooks into the engine. They run with elevated 'editor' capability granting access to the scene graph, asset database, and build pipeline.

**Example: Editor extension adding a custom panel**
```js
import { Extension } from 'editor/core/Extension.js';
import { Panel } from 'editor/ui/Panel.js';

class TerrainEditor extends Extension {
  id = 'terrain-editor';
  capabilities = ['editor', 'scene'];
  
  activate(context) {
    // Add menu item
    context.menus.add('Tools/Terrain', () => this.open());
    
    // Register tool
    context.tools.register('terrain', {
      icon: 'mountain',
      onSelect: (entity) => this.edit(entity)
    });
  }
  
  open() {
    this.panel = new Panel({
      title: 'Terrain Editor',
      content: this.buildUI()
    });
    context.workspace.addPanel(this.panel);
  }
  
  edit(entity) {
    const terrain = entity.get(TerrainComponent);
    this.panel.bind(terrain);
  }
}

editor.extensions.register(TerrainEditor);
```

**See also:** [Editor Overview](/editor/overview.md)
